milestone.description: One map that zooms smoothly, drawn the way the sheets are. This milestone holds only the steps to it, in order; the plan is #129. The classic map's features follow in v2.x.

issues.body:
Part of the plan in #129, after #157.

- Each drawing shows from its own zoom up to the next one's. Between them the page cuts from one drawing to the next, with a short cross-fade only where a cut jars. No morphing between shapes. Practice on existing maps is fixed levels, each enlarged until the next takes over (Dumont, Touya and Duchêne, [More is less](https://josis.org/index.php/josis/article/download/277/184), JOSIS 27, 2023).
- Line widths and type sizes follow the zoom smoothly. Rail spacing follows the zoom the way the test (#154) settled.
- Things that come in at a zoom (stops, street names) grow in over about half a zoom, and names follow their marks.
- The snap to five sheets goes. The buttons ease one zoom. Taps, picking a route, the page's address and the whole-district view work at any zoom.
- Drawings stay as GeoJSON files, fetched as needed. Cloudflare Pages does not answer partial-file requests (checked on the live site), so one tile archive read in ranges will not work there as it is.

What MapLibre 6.15 does between whole zooms, which shapes the above: filters, and layout properties other than text and icon size, are worked out at whole zooms only; paint properties, text size and icon size follow the zoom; a layer's zoom limits can be fractional. Which side a name sits on, and its wording, cannot change between whole zooms.

**Done when** on a phone, in both themes, zooming from the whole district to the closest drawing never shows rail packs pulled apart or overlapping, or lettering at the wrong size, and every control works at a fractional zoom.

Part of the plan in #129, after the test (#154) and the sizes (#155).

Each drawing places its lettering fresh, so the same name can sit on different sides at neighbouring zooms. Measured between drawings a quarter zoom apart (12 and 12.25): 19 of 67 station names change side, and 26 of 54 line letters and 175 of 671 route-number lists move more than 40 px or go.

The change: the build places lettering from the widest zoom inward. A station name, line letter, route-number list or street name keeps the side and place it had one zoom out, unless it no longer fits there. A name on screen does not vanish while zooming in. This follows Been, Daiches and Yap, [Dynamic Map Labeling](https://cs.nyu.edu/visual/home/pub/infovis06.pdf) (IEEE TVCG 12(5), 2006): placing and choosing are done ahead of time, and each label is shown over one unbroken range of zooms.

Today's sheets disagree with one another, so some lettering on them will move. Lettering is touchy: in the redraw trials a change of 3 to 5% in rail width was enough to flip three or four station names. Chris reviews the changed sheets on his phone.

**Done when** the counts above are reported again between every pair of neighbouring drawings, every name, letter or list that still changes has its reason given (it no longer fits), and Chris has signed off today's five sheets as redrawn, in both themes.

issues.body:
Part of the plan in #129: the groundwork for every later step. No visible change. It starts after v1.0 closes, because it changes the build the launch depends on.

Today:

- The build's table of sizes (`SIZES` in `scripts/lib/sheets.mjs`) has 75 sizes, and 21 of them have a value per sheet.
- The page (`public/js/sheets/style.js`) keeps 13 per-sheet tables of its own. Five repeat the build's: rail width, gap, name size and small letter size exactly, number size nearly.
- The build asks which sheet it is drawing in 15 places and the page in about 36: stops, street names, stop tables, which stations are named, which street set, line weights.

The change:

- Each size is a function of zoom that runs straight between today's five values, so a drawing at one of today's zooms is the same as now.
- Each "which sheet" switch becomes a zoom at which the thing comes in.
- The page reads its sizes from the build's output instead of keeping copies.
- `drawSheet` takes any zoom from the widest sheet to the closest.

From redraw trials on sheets 0 to 3 (2026-11-18, build 8828c8b), for whoever picks this up:

- Seven tables are one rule already (`pickApart`, `pickFar`, `round`, `letterDisc`, `pickStub`, `pickBridge`, `nameLetter`). Moving them to a fitted rule changes nothing that can be seen.
- Nine fit a smooth rule within 4 to 14% (`rail`, `gap`, `name`, `letterClear`, `letterEvery`, `busTurn`, `busLabelSize`, `busLabelEvery`, `pickSmooth`), but moving them onto it re-places lettering: rail width on its rule puts three or four station names on another side on sheets 2 and 3. So today's values stay as the stops.
- `busMerge` (4, 4, 7, 7, 24) does not fit a rule. The far and near street sets are a real change of drawing: swapping them moves 11 to 18% of the bus ink, by up to 16 to 37 px.
- None of the 15 tidying passes can be dropped. Switching any one off changes at least one sheet.

issues.title: Test on zoom 12 to 14: rail spacing set by the page, and names that keep their place

milestone.title: v2: One zoomable map
milestone.description: One map that zooms smoothly, drawn the way the sheets are. This milestone holds only the steps to it, in order; the plan is #129. The classic map's features follow in v2.x.

issues.body:
Step 1 of the plan in #129. Two unknowns decide how the zoomable map is built. Both are tested on one stretch, zoom 12 to 14, before anything else is built. Nothing from this test goes to main.

**Rail spacing.** The build sets rail lines side by side in the geometry, at each sheet's pixel scale. Held between two sheets, the packs pull apart above a sheet's zoom and overlap below it. The test: the build draws one rounded centre line for each stretch of shared track and gives each line its slot; the page moves each line sideways by slot times spacing with `line-offset`, and the spacing follows the zoom. `line-offset` takes one amount per feature, so each change of slot is its own piece. What to look at, at fractional zooms: corners, the places where a line joins or leaves a pack, and the ends of shared track. Station bars and line letters have to follow the same slots.

If the corners do not hold, the fallback is rail drawn by the build at half-zoom steps (rail, bars, letters and names are 16 to 26 KB gzipped per drawing), with a correction in the page of a pixel or less.

**Names.** Each drawing places its lettering fresh. Between drawings a quarter zoom apart (12 and 12.25), 19 of 67 station names change side. The test: the build places station names from the wider zoom inward, and a name keeps its side and place unless it no longer fits there. This is the consistency rule of Been, Daiches and Yap, [Dynamic Map Labeling](https://cs.nyu.edu/visual/home/pub/infovis06.pdf) (IEEE TVCG 12(5), 2006): a label does not vanish while zooming in and does not jump.

**Done when** Chris has seen both on his phone through the review page, zooming between 12 and 14, and has picked the way rail spacing is done; and the number of station names that change side between quarter-zoom steps from 12 to 14 is reported before and after.

milestone.title: v2: One zoomable map
milestone.description: One map that zooms smoothly, drawn the way the sheets are. This milestone holds only the steps to it, in order; the plan is #129. The classic map's features follow in v2.x.

issues.body:
The goal after the sheets launch (Chris, 2026-11-13): turn the four fixed-zoom sheets into one map that zooms smoothly, drawn the way the sheets are, and carry over what the classic map has that the sheets don't (route panel, edge letters, relief, route tracing, Live).

The classic map is paused until then.

## The plan (2026-11-18)

v2 ends when the map zooms smoothly. The classic map's features follow in v2.x. Faults written against the classic map's own drawing are in the Parked milestone and are rechecked before v2 is signed off (#161).

The steps, in order. Each is an issue in this milestone:

1. #154 Test on zoom 12 to 14: rail spacing set by the page, and names that keep their place. It touches nothing on main, so it can run before the launch.
2. #155 Sizes follow the zoom, with today's five sheets unchanged. This and the steps after it wait for v1.0 to close.
3. #156 Lettering keeps its place from one zoom to the next.
4. #157 The whole zooms between the sheets drawn: 11, 13 and 15.
5. #158 The page: one map that zooms smoothly through the drawings.
6. #159 Checks for a map with no fixed zooms.
7. #160 Chris's phone review, one band of zoom at a time.
8. #161 Close v2: recheck the parked faults, sign-off and tag.

Then, in v2.x, in an order Chris sets: edge letters (#31), relief (#108), the route panel, route tracing and Live (#162), route panel times (#22), and other times and Live (#11 to #13).

Estimates follow step 1, which settles how rail spacing is done.

## What the plan rests on

From probes and redraw trials on the build at 8828c8b, MapLibre 6.15's documentation, and published work on maps that zoom:

- The build already draws at any zoom: `drawSheet` draws 11, 12.5, 13 and 15 unchanged. Of its 21 sizes with a value per sheet, 16 follow one rule of zoom. What truly differs between sheets is how close two streets must be to be drawn as one, the two street sets, and the switches for stops, street names and which stations are named.
- Held between two sheets, bus streets and route lists still sit right. Rail packs, station bars and line letters break, because the build sets rail lines side by side at each sheet's pixel scale.
- Each drawing places its lettering fresh: between drawings a quarter zoom apart (12 and 12.25), 19 of 67 station names change side. Lettering that keeps its place is the main work.
- MapLibre works out label layout and filters at whole zooms only, while line widths and type sizes can follow the zoom. So the drawings sit on whole zooms.
- Existing maps use fixed levels, each enlarged until the next takes over, then a cut (Dumont, Touya and Duchêne, [More is less](https://josis.org/index.php/josis/article/download/277/184), JOSIS 27, 2023). For lettering, Been, Daiches and Yap, [Dynamic Map Labeling](https://cs.nyu.edu/visual/home/pub/infovis06.pdf) (IEEE TVCG 12(5), 2006): it is placed ahead of time, so a name does not vanish or jump while zooming in.
- DESIGN.md ("Made for continuous zoom later") says drawing between sheets changes the page, not the build. The probes show the build changes too: the lettering, and the drawings in between. DESIGN.md is corrected when step 1 settles the design.

comments.body:
Plan written: eight steps in order, #154 to #161. The classic map's features moved to v2.x and faults in the classic drawing to Parked, so this milestone holds only the path to the zoomable map.

Downtown, 15th and 17th carry about eighteen routes between them, and they join and leave the two streets block by block. Sheet 3 now labels 15th with one row of sixteen numbers, turned with the street, about half a phone's diagonal long. 17th carries almost the same list and is unlabelled at the same view. The long row is also misleading on the street: a local bus stops only every third block there, at stops RTD marks X, Y or Z, so any one stop serves only a third of the routes in the row.

RTD's data already groups them. Stop names on these streets end "[ X Stop ]", "[ Y Stop ]" or "[ Z Stop ]", and each group is a short list (today: X 1 15 15L 20; Y 10 28 32 38 43 44; Z 0 6 8 9 19 48 52 83). RTD's schedules tell riders which letter their bus serves.

The build places it beside the streets, clear of rail, bus lines and route numbers, ahead of district and basemap street names.
- **Sheet 2:** the same table where it fits; otherwise the pair carries no numbers there, and the routes that branch off keep theirs.
- **Sheet 4:** each lettered stop shows its letter, so a rider can find the block their bus stops on.
- **Tap:** the card for one of these streets or stops lists its routes by letter, not as one row.

Nothing names a street, route or letter in the code: the groups come from the stop names in RTD's data, and a street whose stops carry no letters is labelled as it is today.

milestone.title: Launch (v1.0)
milestone.description: What has to be true before the site is called launched and tagged v1.0: the four sheets signed off by Chris on his phone in both themes, a route highlight on the sheets, and #14 (share links, screen reader, offline). Decided 2026-11-13; no domain for v1.0 (2026-11-14).

issues.body:
From Chris, 12 November. The map has grown hard to finish and hard to hand over: faults keep appearing between zooms, and the checks don't catch what he sees on his phone. The direction from here:

**The product, at minimum, is four finished maps you can pan around on a phone.** Each is drawn for one fixed zoom, like a printed sheet. Each covers every route. Each has to look as if it was drawn by an artist who is also a transit planner. Moving between them is a jump from one sheet to the next. A smooth zoom between them comes later.

| Sheet | Zoom | A phone shows about | It answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Opening | 10 | 23 km across | Where the network goes and where service is frequent |
| 2. City | 12 | 6 km | Which lines serve this part of town; route numbers |
| 3. Neighbourhood | 14 | 1.4 km | Which street the bus is on; one-way pairs apart; stations |
| 4. Street | 16 | 360 m | Where the stop is |

**How it is built**
- Mobile first: every size is in phone pixels and every proof is a phone-size capture, dark and light.
- One drawing procedure driven by scale, run once per sheet. No rule is written for one place or one sheet, so a data change redraws all four and more sheets can be added between them later.
- Each sheet has one plain table of what it draws and at what size. Nothing changes between sheets except at a sheet.
- Names and line letters are placed when the map is built, not left to the moment.
- It is built beside the current page (a small viewer and one build step, branch `sheets`), reading the same build output, so it doesn't disturb the live site or the work in progress on other branches.

**Order:** sheet 1 first, because it is what opens. The faults Chris saw on it are in #114. Then sheets 2, 3 and 4. Every sheet has to look designed, not only free of faults (Chris, 12 November: "All of it has to look designed").

**Done when:** Chris opens the preview on his phone and each of the four sheets looks finished to him, in both themes, with every route on it.

Estimate: 600 min of agent time

Ready for a phone look: https://sheets.rtd-system-map.pages.dev/sheets/ (branch `sheets`, 8ef0b87). Needed from Chris: open it on the phone, step through the four sheets with + and −, in dark and light, and say what still looks wrong.

Verified on the deployed preview at phone size (393×760, Chromium), dark: sheet 1 opening view, sheet 2 downtown, sheet 3 Union Station, sheet 4 downtown; all load with no failed requests. Light and other places (Boulder, Aurora, the southeast line ends, the airport) were checked on the same code served locally, not on the preview. Not checked on a real phone.

**Why rail broke below zoom 10** (d956c00)
- MapLibre's GeoJSON tiling drops any part of a line shorter than its tolerance (0.375 px) at the tile's whole zoom.
- The build eases a line across slots in parts a fraction of a pixel long, so at tile zoom 9, G, B and A stopped short of Union Station. W also broke near Auraria West, and C at I-25 / Broadway.
- The fix is `tolerance: 0` on the routes source. For the sheets: any line built from many short eased parts needs either no simplification or parts longer than a pixel at the zoom it's drawn.

**The knot at Union** (0a658a0)
- The track geometry is in real metres: packed within 20 m and rounded over 60 m. At zoom 10, where 1 px is about 60 m, Union's real tracks and bends became jogs smaller than a line's width, so the lines tangled.
- What worked was a second, generalised set below 11: tracks within 350 m packed as one, bends rounded over 1 km. Station ticks and letters sit on that set.
- W leaves at Auraria at a right angle, so it needed a rule to take the side it leaves on, or it wraps around C and E.

**Union Station's marker** (0a658a0, 6100019, 3b2a185)
- The black disc, then a ring, both read as a hole. Chris suggested one ordinary station mark, and that worked.
- On the generalised set, the light rail (C, E, W) ends about 280 m from the commuter lines (A, B, G, N), beside them along the bar. Chris spotted that a bar sized for the commuter four missed W.
- A bar seven lines wide was too long: at zoom 10 the 280 m is under one line spacing, so the two groups mostly overlap. Sizing it from the outermost line end to the other, with their offsets, at the zoom the phones open (10) gave about 4.25 lines' width.
- On a sheet at a fixed zoom this is simpler: measure the line ends in phone pixels and draw the bar across them. That fits your "station bars square to the lines, ending lines curving into their bar".

**The steep bend north of Union at 9 to 9.5** (f5f090c)
- A, B and G eased out of the pack too sharply. The ease had to finish by the first station along, about 1 km on, which is 9 px at zoom 9.
- The generalised set now eases on past stations. Rule of thumb: a move of one line spacing needs about 3 to 4 spacings of length (0.6 px sideways per px).

**Also on that branch:** a double tap zooms in and opens nothing (3b2a185, public/js/select.js). That's independent of #115, and worth keeping wherever the map takes taps.

3. In light, the pale rail lines (R lime, G gold, A light blue) fade into the cream, and white station dots on them vanish. Fix: the same contrast floor, with a thin dark casing where hue can't hold it.

**Places and names**
4. Sheets 1 and 2 name Thornton, Niwot and Highlands Ranch, but never Denver, Aurora, Lakewood or Boulder. Sheet 3 names "Quality Hill Historic District", not Capitol Hill. Fix: place towns first by rank, over bus streets on their halo; on sheets 3–4 prefer neighbourhood names over historic districts.
5. Street names go to side streets (West 14th Avenue, Pine Street), not the streets the buses are on (Colfax, Wadsworth, Broadway). They are long OSM forms at about 2:1 contrast, and float mid-block on sheet 4. Fix: name bus streets first, in short forms, on the centreline, at about 3:1.
6. Bus hubs and Flatiron Flyer stations are unnamed (Downtown Boulder's hall is a bare rectangle); Boulder has no mark on sheets 1–2. Fix: every hall and bus station gets a mark and a name on every sheet, placed by the rail-station rules.
7. Union Station doesn't read as the hub. Sheet 3: two bars about 60 px apart with the hall between them, not linked. Sheet 4: name over the hall. Sheet 2: name about 60 px from its bar. 9. On sheet 4 buildings and streets are the same tone in both themes, so figure and ground swap, and parks barely show in dark. Fix: a minimum lightness gap between ground, street, building and park in each theme.
10. Freeways are too heavy in light and invisible in dark, so "I-25" floats alone. Fix: one quiet step above the ground in both themes, under the quietest bus.

16. On sheets 1–2 a fan of bus streets runs into the hub where the rail lines meet. Fix: bus streets end a rim's width short of a station bar or hall.

Dragging down on the map in iPhone Safari pulls the page and reloads it, losing the view. Chris asked for it gone (2026-11-12).

DESIGN.md already says so ("Nothing that reads as a browser": no rubber-band bounce and no pull-to-refresh, `overscroll-behavior: none`; decision log 2026-11-07), but no commit on any branch ever set `overscroll-behavior: none` in `public/css/app.css`. Only the panels have `overscroll-behavior: contain`.

**What**
- `overscroll-behavior: none` on `html` and `body`, and whatever else iOS Safari needs so a downward drag that starts on the map, the search bar or the Key never pulls the page. The map itself already takes its own touches.
- Panels keep `contain`, so their own scrolling works and doesn't leak to the page.
- Check the other tells in that section of DESIGN.md (tap flash, long-press callout, double-tap delay, zoom on focus) actually shipped too, and file any that didn't.

**Done when** on an iPhone, in Safari and as an installed web app, a drag down from the top of the map, the search bar and the Key never reloads the page, in both themes; and panels still scroll.

Estimate: 20 min of agent time

The fix for the broken lines is on branch `hub-far-zoom` (d956c00, rebased onto main). The hub mark and the knot are still open: see the options and the close-up faults below.

**What was wrong below zoom 10**
- **Lines broke at Union Station.** The map tiles the rail data, and tiling throws away pieces of line shorter than about 0.4 px. Where rail eases from one slot to the next, the pieces are that short at zoom 9 to 10, so they were dropped and the lines broke.
- **The hub showed as a black disc.** Between 9 and 10 the hub had no ring, only its filled disc, and that disc hid line ends.

**Fixed on the branch**
- The rail data is tiled without simplification, so lines stay whole.
- Two new checks:
  - `ends/break`: a line cut in two.
  - `ends/end-hidden`: a line end hidden under a mark.
- The checks now run from zoom 9, in 0.25 steps. The opening zooms (9.99 on 402x655, 10.11 on 390x844) now sit between drawing thresholds.
- Verified on captures at zooms 9 to 10.5 in 0.25 steps, both themes, both sizes. Model findings at zooms 9 to 10.5:

  | | `break` | `end-hidden` |
  |---|---|---|
  | main | 19 | 24 |
  | this branch | 0 | 0 |

- `npm test`: 359 passed.
- `check:recall`: 10 of 10 finds on e2bae25 are caught, including 103-broadway-break, now caught by `break`. Nothing scored worse.

**The black disc: options at the opening view**

Rows are 402x655 and 390x844, light and dark:
- **A:** an open ink ring.
- **B:** no hub mark; the lines meeting and the name do the work.

![options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datapolitical/rtd-system-map/captures-115/sheet-close.png)

I also tried a ring and a soft glow drawn under the tracks. The rail's casing hides both, so neither is an option.

Neither A nor B fixes the real fault at the opening view: **the lines themselves tangle at Union.** They jog and wiggle, and W wraps around C and E. A mark on top can't fix that. I'm working on the knot next: the lines should come into Union as one calm, even pack and split cleanly. Once the knot is clean, B (no mark) is likely enough, and I'll show it again then.

**Close up, dark theme** ([z11](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datapolitical/rtd-system-map/captures-115/close-dark-z11.png), [z12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datapolitical/rtd-system-map/captures-115/close-dark-z12.png), [z13](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datapolitical/rtd-system-map/captures-115/close-dark-z13.png)):
- **At 11 to 12, Union's two platform marks overlap.** `marks-overlap` finds this: 67% overlap at 11, 28% at 12.
- **At 11, station marks crowd where W splits off south of Union.** They touch, with the W letter on top of them.
- **In dark, station marks are near-black with a thin edge,** so at these sizes they read as holes in the lines.
- From 13 the two platforms joined by the dotted transfer read cleanly.

The black ring is gone, and the lines into Union Station are cleaner (branch `hub-far-zoom`, 0a658a0). - **Hub:** Union Station is an ordinary station tick across all its lines, like every other station. - **Lines into Union:** below zoom 11 the rail is drawn from a second, simpler set of tracks. Tracks within 350 m share one pack, and bends are rounded over a kilometre. MED = clearly ugly or against DESIGN.md; LOW = polish.

9. MED G has a sharp zigzag before the B/G split (west of Pecos Junction); smooth close in.

11. MED R meets E/T in a sharp V with a blunt end (I-225 junction north of Belleview).

## B. Union Station
12. HIGH Look-alike colours line up through the hub (W-A teal/sky, C-G orange/gold, E-N purple/magenta): it reads as three through lines. No letter within 60 px.

milestone.title: v2.x: Classic features, other times and Live

issues.body:
The relief (hillshade and elevation tint, `TERRAIN` in `public/js/basemap.js`) is the largest download on the site, and its tiles compete with the network and basemap for the connection.

Measured 2026-11-12 on the live site (headless Chromium, Pixel 7, 170 ms / 9 Mbps, `qa/perf/load.mjs`):
- Opening view: about 896 KB of elevation tiles from `s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod`, against about 631 KB for the whole site (page, MapLibre, data, font).
- A short pan and zoom after that: another 2.5 MB of elevation tiles.
- They come over HTTP/1.1 from S3, a separate connection, uncached by our service worker's rules for our own files. The DEM source goes to `maxzoom: 12`; terrarium PNGs are 110 to 135 KB each at z11 and z12.

Today the relief is added when the `routes` source has loaded. Stations, streets, labels and basemap tiles can still be loading then.

Plan:
1. **Load it last** (Chris, 2026-11-12): add the relief only once the map is fully drawn (`idle`) after the network has loaded, so nothing it fetches competes with the system map.
2. **Fewer, smaller tiles**: a lower DEM maxzoom (MapLibre overzooms the DEM; the relief is meant to be soft and fades out by zoom 14). Compare 12, 11, 10 and 9 with `qa/perf/relief-zooms.mjs` at the opening view, zoom 10, the foothills at Golden (12), the Flatirons (13) and Morrison (14), both themes, and pick the lowest that still looks like the mountains.
3. **Maybe our own copy**: the build fetches the few tiles the district needs at that maxzoom and serves them from the site (HTTP/2, same connection, kept offline by the service worker), falling back to S3 if the fetch fails. Only if 1 and 2 leave it worth it.

Done when: the opening view's elevation bytes and the bytes from a pan and zoom are both well down, the relief arrives after the network is drawn, and captures of the views above look right in both themes (DESIGN.md, "Relief").

Estimate: 120 min of agent time

issues.body:
From Chris's review of the live map on 11 November.

**What is wrong**

- Alameda: "the buses aren't literally on top of the rail so that makes no sense." The bus lane beside the platform is within the width the three rail lines are drawn at, so the bus line is hidden under them and its five stop dots sit on the rail. [Open](https://rtd-system-map.pages.dev/#17/39.7080/-104.9925)
- Union Station: the light rail "overlaps the bus routes in a way that a hand drawn map wouldn't". The bus line along the light-rail platform touches the E line, and a bus line ends in a round blob against it at the concourse's edge. [Open](https://rtd-system-map.pages.dev/#16.5/39.7551/-105.0030)

**Cause.** Rail lines sharing track are drawn side by side at a fixed width on screen, so a pack of three is about 53 m wide on the ground at zoom 15, 29 m at 16 and 14 m at 17. A bus street within that of the track is drawn where RTD draws it, under the pack. A scan of main (3e38acb, comment below) found 105 such stretches, 43 km in all.

**Approach** (replaces "rail keeps its place"; Chris, 11 November: "in some cases we might need to nudge the rail line because in some cases the rail line is in the wrong place, in some cases the bus is in the wrong place, in some cases they are on top of each other … there's not an easy obvious single use solution here"). The bar is that every view looks intentional and hand-drawn.

1. For each stretch, find what is true on the ground, from OpenStreetMap's track and road centrelines beside RTD's lines:
   - *rail in the wrong place*: RTD's track, or the pack's middle, is off the real track. Nudge the rail onto it (DESIGN.md "Shared track" already allows tens of metres).
   - *bus in the wrong place*: RTD's bus line is off the real street or lane. Move the bus onto it.
   - *really side by side*: a bus lane beside a platform, a street beside the track. Draw them side by side on purpose: the bus kept a fixed gap clear of the pack at every zoom, with its stops, eased in and out where it joins and leaves, the way a hand-drawn map shows a street beside a railway.
   - *really on top of each other*: bus and rail on one right of way. Decide with Chris, by pictures, which reads better.
2. Build the rule for each kind from the data (no place listed by name); a place no rule draws well goes to the fixes file (#64), tied to RTD's data.
3. Judge by pictures: each changed place at zoom 13 to 18 in both themes, before and after, against DESIGN.md's rubric ("drawn on purpose"). Counts from checks are not the measure.
4. Start with Alameda and Union Station's light rail; post before and after to Chris and wait for his answer before merging; then the rest by kind.

**Done when:** at Alameda and at Union Station's light rail, at zoom 15 to 17 in both themes, no bus line or bus stop is drawn on a rail line it only runs beside, and the route check reports no new fault against main.

Estimate: 300 min of agent time

Measured before building: this is the whole network, not two places. On main's build (3e38acb), 105 stretches of bus street, 43 km in all, run along a rail line within 40 m of it. The plan below treats them all by one rule.

**What the scan found** (stretches 40 m or longer, bus street within 30 degrees of the rail's direction):
- On the same street as the rail: 15L on Abilene with the R line (559 m, 0.6 m apart), AT beside the E and R lines for 2.5 km (3 m apart as RTD draws them), 11 on Exposition (491 m, 5 m).

2. Draw those stretches offset in pixels by zoom, like rail lines sharing track: just enough at each zoom to clear the pack, and nothing once the pack no longer reaches the street. Ease the offset in and out over the ends of the stretch. A street that crosses rail is not touched.
3. Stops on those stretches are drawn with the same offset, so they stay on their bus line.
4. The route lines behind the part-time routes, the route numbers and the tap highlight follow the same offsets, or the route check's street-alignment rule will report every stretch.
5. Checks: a detector for a bus line or stop drawn on a rail line it runs beside, pinned first on Alameda and Union Station in `qa/recall/finds.json`.

issues.body:
Decided by Chris, 2026-11-10.

DESIGN.md says every visual cleanup must be a rule in the build that works on any network, "never a hand edit of one spot". That is right for facts. For looks it forces a general algorithm for a single place: on `union-building` the platform-group logic notes that "only Union Station has more than one group".

The rule is narrowed:

- **Facts are never hand-set:** routes, stations, frequencies, colors, names, what stops where. They come from RTD's data on every build, as now.
- **A visual fix for one named place is allowed,** in one small file the build reads. Each fix names its place by RTD's own ids and records a fingerprint of the geometry it was written for. If RTD changes that place, the fix is skipped and the build log says so, so a stale fix can never draw.
- A fix may move or reshape what is drawn within the limits "It looks designed" already sets (some meters, never onto another street or past a station). It cannot add, remove or rename anything.
- A general rule is still preferred where one place is an instance of a pattern.

*Done when:* DESIGN.md ("Zero maintenance", "Shared track") states the narrowed rule; the build reads the file, skips and reports a fix whose place has changed, and a test covers both cases.

comments.body: Root cause found: the check read the view before the page placed the edge letters. The page places them on the map's idle, and after a teleport MapLibre can draw a dozen frames on GitHub's runner without ever firing idle, so a 700 ms quiet spell read the view mid-work. The check now forces a frame and waits until the letters stop arriving, up to three rounds (qa/lib/inpage.js). Verifying on the runner now.

Retitled: this is the map, not the check.

What is wrong, and where: at zoom 11.64, 39.59231, -104.8839 (light, the light phone project), line R crosses the screen for 468 px with no letter on it, and the same for a handful of other seeded views in both themes. Open the place: https://rtd-system-map.pages.dev/#11.64/39.59231/-104.8839

The capture is in that run's artifact, `qa/checks/out/letters-twenty-seeded-phon-35970--letter-for-every-rail-line-phone-light/view-4-missing.png` (download with `gh run download 42500880020`).

Why: `public/js/edgeletters.js` places an edge letter only in a `map.once('idle')` callback, and it never retries. On GitHub's runner the map draws frames after a teleport without ever reporting idle (measured: a dozen frames, every tile loaded, no idle event), so the pass never runs and the line keeps no letter until something else draws a later frame. On a Mac the same check passed 20/20, so this is a slow-renderer hole, not a wrong drawing.

issues.title: Whole-network line ordering in busbundles and sharedtrack

milestone.title: Later
milestone.description: Ideas with no date: places worth going, Spanish, design-document and research follow-ups.

issues.body:
Port LOOM's idea, not its code (GPL), as a deterministic JS pass in `sharedTrack`. Run it after each bundle's order is ranked and before slots are assigned:

1. Build the line graph: each bundle is an edge, and handovers between runs are nodes. This is `toLoom` in the benchmark's `graph.mjs`.
2. Score with LOOM's penalty: same-segment crossings ×4, fork crossings ×1, separations ×3. This is the benchmark's `score.py`.
3. Hill-climb: start from today's orders, and keep any move of a line to another position that lowers the penalty at the bundle's two end nodes. Respect no-stubs and `driftSlots`.
4. Add a rule flag, on for buses. Rail must stay 0 / 0 / 1.

Bar: the build's crossings stay at 9 or fewer, and the pass adds less than 1 s to the build. The before/after captures at Civic Center, 16th & California, I-25/Broadway and Federal & Colfax must look better, not just score better. Expected gain is about 8 fewer crossings and 13 fewer separations, mostly downtown (#15).

Starts after the bus job merges. Brief: `rtd-references/loom-benchmark/PORT-BRIEF.md`.

Estimate: 150 min of agent time

comments.body:
What to port from LOOM (Bast, Brosi & Storandt, [SIGSPATIAL 2018](https://ad-publications.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/SIGSPATIAL_transitmaps_2018.pdf), [code](https://github.com/ad-freiburg/loom)), if #15 shows it orders lines better than step 4 of `busbundles.mjs` / `sharedtrack.mjs`. Our step 4 orders lines one pair at a time; LOOM orders the whole network at once with an ILP:

- **Separation penalty:** lines that run together, part, and run together again pay a cost, so partners stay side by side.
- **Periphery condition:** a line that ends at a station sits at the edge of its pack, never mid-pack (the "no stubs" rule, enforced by the optimizer).
- **Crossings away from stations:** crossings at station nodes are weighted high enough that they always land between stations.
- **Core-graph pruning** keeps the ILP small (2–4× smaller in the paper):
  1. merge degree-2 nodes whose two edges carry the same lines
  2. collapse lines that always run together into one weighted line
  3. drop edges whose ends are termini for all their lines

**Implementation:** reimplement in JS (`scripts/lib/lineorder.mjs`), not by vendoring LOOM's GPL-3.0 C++ into the build. `highs-js` (HiGHS compiled to WASM) can solve it inside `npm run build`, keeping Rules 1 and 2. Unit-test it on a made-up network first.

The Transit app reached the same conclusion: ordering by where lines end only worked in places, and they moved to an ILP ([Dubrau 2016](https://blog.transitapp.com/how-we-built-the-worlds-prettiest-auto-generated-transit-maps-12d0c6fa502f)). Where crossings can't be avoided downtown, consider block crossings ([Fink, Pupyrev & Wolff 2015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0069)).
Benchmark says go (−16% penalty, #15); the plan is scoped in the body, and it starts after the bus job merges.

milestone.description: Not a release, and not planned work. Faults and leftovers written against the classic map's drawing, which the zoomable map (v2) replaces. Each is rechecked on the zoomable map before v2 is signed off: one that still shows becomes a new issue, the rest close.

issues.body:
- The six phone-review findings
- The I-25 triangle
- Steady line widths
- Key rows
- A strand for every route on a shared street (part-time ones dashed)
- Round four, from Chris's phone check of round three:
  - Civic Center: drop the disk. Draw the terminal in the shape of the real building, with its stops placed on it where they really are; streets around it drawn as they are. Update DESIGN.md (Terminals, `bus-terminal`) and its decision log.
  - I-25 ramps by 38th/Fox: dashed strands still wobble and cross where the ramps split, with a squiggle near 31st Street.
  - 17+GS by Colorado Mills: the dashed part-time strand rides the edge of the solid line instead of sitting beside it.
- Shared-street frequency is tracked separately in #131; it is not remaining work in this Classic styling ticket.

Estimate: 120 min of agent time

comments.body: Being built on branch `bundles-round3`.

Round three (dff2e15 on bus-frequency, preview at bus-frequency.rtd-system-map.pages.dev): Knox, Colorado Mills and Federal/Colfax fixed, one arrow glyph. Still not beautiful: the I-25/38th ramp cluster, stop dots inside the Civic Center disk, and the 17+GS street (no room for two strands, and a dark diamond at zoom 16.5). Next: keep routes whole inside highway interchanges, one station shape with lines stopping at its edge, and a minimum strand width at close zoom.
Needs Chris: OK for thin shared streets to get a little wider at close zoom so each route shows as its own line (part-time dashed)?
Chris approved: thin shared streets may widen at close zoom so each route shows as its own line, part-time dashed.
Needs Chris: a phone check of round three at bus-frequency.rtd-system-map.pages.dev before round four starts.

Chris checked round three on the phone: drop the Civic Center disk. Draw the terminal in the shape of the real building (its footprint from OpenStreetMap or the basemap's building layer), with the stops placed on it where they really are. Streets around it drawn accurately, tidied only where lines collide. Update DESIGN.md (Terminals, bus-terminal) and its decision log with that change.
Round four queued on branch `bus-round4` (made from `bus-frequency`): the terminal drawn as its real building, then the rest of the list. It starts when the current heavy job (#19) finishes.

Round four is on branch `bus-round4` (222be2a), preview at https://bus-round4.rtd-system-map.pages.dev.

What changed: a bus terminal is now the building its bus gates stand in, found in OpenStreetMap at build time. Civic Center's 71 x 84 m station and the 171 x 116 m garage over Nine Mile's bays are drawn in the disk's place — filled, ringed in street ink, stops on them where they really are — and the lanes inside them are no longer streets. A terminal with no building of its own (Southwest Plaza, Lincoln / Jordan, Union Station's forecourt) draws nothing at all. A shared street's frequency is now the gap nine gaps in ten are at or under, so two every-30 routes that leave a minute apart read every 30, not every 15; the honest cost is that the top class is now rare, and downtown reads lighter. A part-time route's hairline now sits 2.2 px clear of the street it runs beside.

Still open: the I-25 ramps by 38th/Fox. The dashed express strands still wobble and cross where the ramps split, and the squiggle near 31st Street is still there — 19 runs within 450 m, five of them under 130 m, the shortest 27 m. Fixing it means changing how a route's line is generalized through an interchange, which I did not want to do at the end of a session without the pictures to judge it by.

The preview had not come up when I finished (404 after 25 minutes of polling on a new branch), so it may need a redeploy.

Not ready for a phone check after all: compared with satellite imagery, Nine Mile is drawn as the parking garage rather than its bus platforms, Union Station's underground concourse (in OSM as amenity=bus_station) was missed, and Civic Center's underground hall is drawn as if above ground. The fixes go into branch `union-building` (#19 round two), which carries round four.
Being fixed by the union-building agent (#19): Nine Mile drawn from its bus platforms, Civic Center drawn below ground, Union Station's bus concourse added.
Round 4 on `union-building` also fixes bus lines through freeway interchanges, rush-hour dashes that leave their line, and widths that jump near stations: items 6 to 8 of the instructions on #19.

Chris's phone check of the `union-building` preview found faults at the 15th Street corner by Comedy Works, Nine Mile and Union Station, listed in #42. Round four should fix them; they are also the first fixtures for the new checks (milestone "Checks that see what a phone sees").
Not in progress: the classic map is paused until the sheets work (2026-11-13).
Counting a shared street's frequency by gaps moved to #131 (Launch). What's left here is Classic map styling and its dashed part-time strands, so it moves to After launch.
Correction: the milestones were redrawn on 13 November (DESIGN.md, the roadmap after launch), so this sits in "v2: One zoomable map", not "After launch". The frequency count is #131, in v1.1.

Moved to Parked. This is a fault in the classic map's drawing, which the zoomable map (#129) replaces, so it is not planned work. It is rechecked on the zoomable map before v2 is signed off: if it still shows it becomes a new issue, otherwise it closes.
